encodingNote: Strict JSON cannot encode NaN/Infinity; the nonfinite vector therefore uses the string token "NaN" as the field value. A consumer must treat any non-numeric value in a numeric field as invalid data (unavailable), never as zero.
notice: SYNTHETIC TEST VECTORS — not source data. These cases never occur in the pinned fixture (verified 2026-10-20: all 582 real rows carry all 8 projected fields as finite numbers, with no duplicate athlete IDs and no duplicate stat names). They exist so a grader consumer can test its absent/null/invalid handling. GP boundary cases (19/20/39/40) DO occur in the real extract and are listed in the issue comment instead of being duplicated here.

vectors.expect: unavailable (invalid data), not zero-filled, not unscored-by-absence
unavailable (invalid data); null is preserved by the projection and is distinct from an absent key and from 0
unavailable (invalid data); a non-numeric token in a numeric field is never parsed as a number and never treated as zero

projection-level hard error: the extractor aborts on duplicate IDs, so a consumer should never receive this; if it constructs one by hand, behavior must be an explicit error, not first-wins or last-wins
UNSCORED: an ID with no row at all (e.g. 5107157, a 2026 rookie with no 2025-26 line) is a missing-coverage result with its own explanation, distinct from the invalid-data cases above
